Q: iOS [Transporter] - executable references an unsupported platform in the arm64 slice A: 
dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter

  path_provider_foundation: 2.5.1

path_provider_foundation 2.6.0 introduced a dependency on objective_c 9.3.0, which uses native assets (FFI). The objective_c framework was being built with the IOSSIMULATOR platform marker instead of IOS, even in release builds. App Store Connect correctly rejects binaries with simulator platform markers.

Q: GPT4All fails to load CUDA backend on RTX 2050, kompute device not working A:

the CUDA DLL errors are just warnings, not what blocks kompute. GPU is only used when the kompute backend for your platform and model actually works, and on Windows that’s currently limited to certain GGUF quantizations and sizes.
Try a smaller 7B Q4_0 model on the latest GPT4All; if that still stays on CPU, your GPU/model combo simply isn’t supported yet and there isn’t a missing CUDA dependency you can install to fix it.

Q: Invoke-Sqlcmd times out after ~30s on some machines but not others (without -QueryTimeout). What determines the default and what’s best practice? A:

AlwaysLearning provided the crucial pointer in a comment on the question:

Your symptom suggests that different machines of yours use different editions of the Invoke-SqlCmd cmdlet and/or possibly outdated versions:

There are two - technically distinct - Invoke-SqlCmd cmdlets:[1]

  • (a) The obsolete Invoke-SqlCmd command from the obsolete SQLPS module.

    • For the sake of backward compatibility, this obsolete module still comes with SSMS.

  • (b) The current Invoke-SqlCmd command from the successor module, SqlServer

    • Only v16.x versions of SSMS came bundled with this module.
    • In v17.x and above, it must be installed on demand from the PowerShell Gallery with, e.g.: Install-Module -Scope CurrentUser SqlServer
      and later upgraded with, e.g.:
      Update-Module -Scope CurrentUser SqlServer

You can tell which version is loaded (implicitly) on a given machine by running the following command in a pristine session, which also reveals the originating module's version number:

(Get-Command Invoke-SqlCmd).Module

Note: If, after installing the modern SqlServer module, the obsolete SqlPs module still surfaces by default, see this answer for troubleshooting and uninstallation instructions.

Default query timeouts:

  • Implementation (a) de facto appears to default to 30 seconds.

    • The official help topic is, as of this writing, malformed and is missing a description of the -QueryTimeout parameter (a description of the command as a whole is presented instead).

    • It's hard to find definitive claims to that effect, but here's a pointer from Troubleshoot query time-out errors:

      • If the query doesn't return any data within the configured time-out value (typically 30 seconds)

  • By contrast, implementation (b) defaults to not timing out, based on the official help topic stating for the -QueryTimeout parameter:

    • If a timeout value is not specified, the queries do not time out.

    • Conceivably, an older version of the SqlServer module also had the 30-second timeout; if so, update to the latest version with, e.g.,
      Update-Module -Scope CurrentUser SqlServer

[1] See SQL Server PowerShell for background information.

Q: Will php mb_strlen($str,‘utf8’) ever return a greater result than JavaScript .length? A:

No, mb_strlen($str,‘utf8’) can never return a value greater than String.length in JavaScript because you are comparing Apples and Oranges and Oranges will always be bigger.

mb_strlen($str,‘utf8’) returns the length of the string in UTF-8 characters.

String.length returns the length of the string in UTF-16 code units. A single UTF-16 character can be composed of 1 or 2 code units. Therefore for a string containing characters composed of multiple code units, it can return a value twice as large as you expect.

This is why if you want to get a length of a string in JavaScript you should almost never use String.length. Use something like. '😀'.split().length

Q: Video input to Shortcuts action A:

It seems that this is a bug in iOS, as doing the exact same things but passing into Apple's own "Save File" action has the same problem.

A workaround I've discovered is to use "Encode Media" in between. But be warned that this loses the metadata (e.g., datetime and location).

Q: Why would anyone use VCL when there is FMX? A:

Same here:

  • Cropping a picture in MS Paint? Select it, then CTRL+C (copy), CTRL+N (new), N (don't save), CTRL+V (paste), CTRL+S (save).
  • I expect comboboxes to open via F4.
  • I expect to automatically "click" a default button (mostly "Ok") by just pressing ENTER when being in a different control.
  • Likewise I use F6 to cycle between window areas (f.e. in Thunderbird between account folders, email lists, and email content).
  • I use CTRL+TAB to switch between tabs/pages and use CTRL+RIGHT to move the text cursor word wise.
  • I also hold down CTRL when clicking on a scrollbar position to get the bar right there (instead of just going one page up).
  • Does drag'n'drop work as in Windows? Dragging an item with the RIGHT mouse button to open the context menu when dropping the item?

No, by far not everything of that is covered by non-native GUIs, especially when it comes to dialog windows. I've experienced quirks with FMX, Qt, MFC, XUL, Perl/Tk, AWT and others - they do their job, but I work fastest and most efficiently (not needing to double check again and again) with Windows' GDI - and Delphi's VCL.

Of course people don't see much difference when using the mouse for everything. But then again I could use CSS right away (although good websites can be used by keyboard alone, too)...
